subject.title: Reply-session init conflict is silently dropped on Slack/webchat/heartbeat inbound, though Telegram already treats it as retryable

question: Should this issue be resolved by landing the shared fenced reply-session-init self-heal first, or should webchat and heartbeat also get explicit retry or visible-failure parity before the issue is considered fixed?
rationale: Current source shows both a shared root conflict throw and surface-specific terminalization; choosing shared recovery versus per-surface retry affects the permanent owner boundary for session lifecycle failures.

options.title: Review Shared Self-Heal First
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920 as the primary fix path, then retest webchat and heartbeat conflict cases after it lands.

options.title: Require Surface Retry Parity
options.body: Keep the shared PR separate and queue explicit webchat and heartbeat retry or coalescing behavior for this conflict class.

options.title: Ask For Live Surface Proof
options.body: Request a current-main live reproduction for the exact webchat or heartbeat path before choosing the repair layer.

recommendation.title: Review Shared Self-Heal First
recommendation.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920 as the primary fix path, then retest webchat and heartbeat conflict cases after it lands.

likelyOwner.reason: jalehman has the strongest recent history on the central guarded reply-session initialization and session-accessor boundary where the owner-boundary choice sits.
